title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'suite à La Longue Marche' notes Grothendieck works with 'L-groupes', discrete or profinite groups equipped with a loop ('lacets') structure. These are fundamental groups of surfaces or orbifolds together with their cusp (puncture) loop classes and an orientation.

(1) The page finishes a remark begun on p. 741. There he calls the group of L-outer automorphisms of an L-group its 'Teichmüller group'. A variant, perhaps better, uses the L-outer automorphisms of the subgroup Π^+ of elements acting directly (orientation-preserving), of index 1 or 2.
- He identifies 𝔖_{0,3} ≅ GL(2,Z)/±1 = PGL(2,Z), the extended modular group.
- Its direct part 𝔖_{0,3}^+ is PSL(2,Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3, the (2,3,∞) triangle group. Its generators are ρ (order 3) and σ (order 2).
- On p. 741 he had shown that the direct Teichmüller group of 𝔖_{0,3}^+ is trivial. He did this by studying surjections onto S_3 = Aut(P^1 − {0,1,∞}), with σ mapping to the transpositions σ_0, σ_1, σ_∞.
- The 'corresponding property' for the full L-group 𝔖_{0,3} is stated here: every L-automorphism of 𝔖_{0,3}^+ is induced by conjugation by a unique element of 𝔖_{0,3}. In modern terms: Aut_L(PSL(2,Z)) = PGL(2,Z), and PSL(2,Z) has trivial centralizer in PGL(2,Z).
- He then conjectures, with 'peut-être', that this rigidity characterizes the discrete L-groups of type (0,3).

(2) He then proposes to reformulate the notion of L-group π. The data are:
- a free Z-module T of rank 1, the 'module of orientations' (a discrete analogue of Ẑ(1));
- a finite set (K_i)_{i∈I} of germs of outer homomorphisms K_i : T → π.
'Germ' means a homomorphism defined on some finite-index subgroup nT, up to restriction (and up to conjugacy, since the maps are outer). This lets one record a cusp loop that only becomes a genuine loop after passing to a power.

On the next page this is carried to a finite-index subgroup Π_0. Effective homomorphisms nT → Π in a class K_i, with image in Π_0, induce a finite set of germs T → Π_0; these correspond to the Π_0-orbits, i.e. the cusps above the given one. The single axiom of an L-structure is that, for some finite-index Π_0, the induced structure comes from a genuine loop structure, i.e. a surface group with its peripheral cusp classes.

So an L-group is a group that is virtually a surface group with peripheral structure. Elliptic (finite-order) points are not recorded as data: they are encoded by torsion, which disappears in Π_0. He then proposes generalizing by dropping the requirement that Π_0 have finite index.

Purpose: to set up an intrinsic, cover-stable group-theoretic language for orbifold fundamental groups with inertia/cusp data. This is the framework needed for the Teichmüller tower and Galois actions in the Longue Marche.
errors: No mathematical error. The isomorphism GL(2,Z)/±1 ≅ PGL(2,Z) and Aut(PSL(2,Z)) ≅ PGL(2,Z), with trivial centralizer, are correct.

The conjectured characterization ('peut-être caractéristique') needs care. For type (0,3) with three cusps (the free group F_2 of P^1−{0,1,∞}), orientation-preserving L-outer automorphisms that permute cusps give S_3, not 1. So triviality holds only for the 'pure' version, or when the three local orders are distinct as for (2,3,∞). With that proviso the statement follows from the Dehn–Nielsen–Baer theorem for orbifolds: the mapping class group is trivial iff Teichmüller space is a point, which happens exactly for type (0,3).

The germ formalism records cusps but not cone points: a germ of a homomorphism on nT into a finite-order element is trivial. Elliptic data are therefore implicit in torsion. This is consistent with the next page's axiom, but the page leaves it unstated.

ideas.what: Teichmüller group of an L-group = group of L-outer automorphisms, or of its direct index-≤2 part Π^+
ideas.modern_name: Extended / pure mapping class group via Out of the orbifold fundamental group (Dehn–Nielsen–Baer)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dehn, Nielsen, Baer; for orbifolds Maclachlan–Harvey, Zieschang
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Teichmüller groups and the Teichmüller tower in this spirit

ideas.what: Every L-automorphism of PSL(2,Z) is induced by a unique element of PGL(2,Z)
Conjecture that trivial (direct) Teichmüller group characterizes discrete L-groups of type (0,3)
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class group trivial iff Teichmüller space is a point (triangle groups / thrice-punctured sphere)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore consequence of Teichmüller theory and Dehn–Nielsen–Baer

ideas.what: Definition of an L-group as a group π with rank-1 orientation module T and a finite set of germs (on finite-index subgroups of T) of outer homomorphisms T → π; axiom: virtually a genuine surface-with-cusps loop structure
ideas.modern_name: Virtual surface group with peripheral structure / orbifold group with cuspidal inertia data; cf. group-theoretic cuspidal inertia in anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: peripheral systems (Waldhausen, Jaco–Shalen); profinite cuspidal structures (Nakamura, Mochizuki)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions discrete/profinite groups with loop structure ('groupes à lacets'); the germ formalism itself is not known to me in print

missed.claim: A cover-stable, intrinsic axiomatization of orbifold (L-)groups in which cusp data are germs of outer homomorphisms from an orientation module T, defined up to finite-index subgroups of T. The single axiom is that the structure becomes a genuine surface loop structure on some finite-index subgroup. This is a tidy formalism, close to later anabelian treatments of cuspidal inertia, but stated here for discrete groups with an explicit 'germ' device.
missed.quote: en termes de la donnée d'un Z-module T libre de rg 1 (le Z-module d'orientations) et d'un ensemble fini (K_i)_{i∈I} de germes d'hom. extérieurs
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly of historical interest. It documents Grothendieck's precise definition of 'groupes à lacets', which Esquisse only names; the content parallels Mochizuki/Nakamura-style cuspidal structures.

deep.surprise_reason: The facts stated are classical (Aut PSL(2,Z) = PGL(2,Z); rigidity of type (0,3)). The germ-based definition of L-groups is a nice unpublished formalization of 'groupes à lacets', but its content matches known notions of peripheral and cuspidal structure.
transcription_corrections: 'en termes de L donnée' should read 'en termes de la donnée'.
The superscript on K_i (transcribed ξ) is uncertain; it may be a 'g' or a 'ξ'.

The opening fragment 'La propriété correspondante' spans pages: p. 741 ends 'La propriété' and this page begins 'correspondants du L-groupe'.
